title: Defamation as a criminal offence - is it still relevant in India
p1:
Can a few words on a screen really lead to a criminal case?

In the age of social media, one post, video, or comment can reach thousands within minutes. But many people are surprised to learn that defamation is not only a civil matter in India; it can also be treated as a criminal offence.
p2:
A common misconception is that freedom of speech means anyone can say anything about anyone. The reality is different. The law protects opinions and criticism, but false statements that harm a person's reputation may have legal consequences.

What many don't know is that criminal defamation does not require the person affected to prove financial loss. Damage to reputation itself can become the basis of a complaint.
p3:
The debate around criminal defamation continues because it involves a delicate balance: protecting individual dignity while ensuring that free expression is not restricted unfairly.

For businesses, professionals, and public figures, this is a reminder that responsible communication matters. A comment made casually today can create serious legal consequences tomorrow.
conclusion: Should India continue treating defamation as a criminal offence, or should reputation-related disputes be handled only through civil remedies?
